To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we can compute a meaningful score linking an image and sentence, that this score can be used for image retrieval, and that the score can be used as a loss function in a training process.
we can automatically generate a description of a picture, and that the resulting descriptions are very similar to those produced by humans.

(1) it is possible to generate sentences that describe images, (2) this is done by comparing an estimateof meaning obtained from the images to one obtained from text, (3) this estimate of meaning is obtained by discriminative learning from data, and (4) this approach produces very good quantitative results.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: How can we automatically compute an estimate of meaning for an image and a sentence?
the question of whether we can generate a description of an image that is concise, accurate, and human-like.
the problem of describing images with sentences and vice versa.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the results are good.

we are able to automatically generate a sentence that describes the content of an image, or to automatically find an image that illustrates a given sentence, and this is done by comparing a meaning representation of an image with one of a sentence.
the method we propose can generate a sentence from an image, and vice versa, and that the results are very good.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a simple, discriminative, meaning estimate is sufficient to produce a very high quality image-to-text retrieval system.
we show that a system can be trained to produce descriptions of images.
we have developed an approach for generating sentences from images and for generating images from sentences, which is based on the notion of meaning.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it shows that it is possible to generate sentences from images, even if the sentences are not always perfect.
it is possible to generate sentences from images that are as good as those generated by humans.
the task of generating sentences from images can be tackled with simple, discriminative procedures.
